# Synthetic Tax & Compliance Knowledge Base

Value-added tax registration in South Africa becomes mandatory once the taxable supplies of an enterprise exceed R1 million in any consecutive 12-month period. Voluntary registration is possible from R50,000. The registration application is filed on the SARS VAT 101 form and the vendor must keep tax invoices for five years.

Provisional tax applies to taxpayers who earn income other than a salary, and returns are submitted twice a year on the IRP6 form. The first provisional period runs for the first six months of the year of assessment and the second period covers the remaining six months, with a third top-up payment for some taxpayers.

The Companies and Intellectual Property Commission requires every registered company to file an annual return within 30 business days of the anniversary of incorporation. Late filing attracts penalties calculated per month of delay, and a company that fails to file for two consecutive years risks deregistration.

Payroll employers must register with the Unemployment Insurance Fund and contribute 2% of each employee's remuneration, split evenly between employer and employee. The monthly EMP201 declaration includes UIF, SDL where applicable, and PAYE, and is due within seven days after the end of the month.

Skills development levy becomes payable when the employer's annual payroll exceeds R500,000. The levy is 1% of the monthly payroll and is declared together with the EMP201. Employers registered with a Sector Education and Training Authority may recover part of the levy through discretionary and mandatory grants.

The Protection of Personal Information Act regulates the processing of personal information by responsible parties. Operators must process data only with the knowledge or authorisation of the responsible party and under a written contract. Cross-border transfers require adequate protection or the data subject's consent.

Management accounts should be prepared monthly and reconciled to the bank statement before any reporting cycle. A standard pack includes an income statement, a balance sheet, a cash-flow statement and a short narrative on material variances against budget.

Record retention: the Tax Administration Act requires taxpayers to keep relevant material for five years from the date of the relevant return. Company records under the Companies Act must be retained for seven years. Where the two periods differ, the longer retention period applies.
